mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-72.6 to -66.7), indicating a steady recovery trend in retail/recreation mobility that should continue as momentum carries forward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased monotonically from -72.6 to -66.7 over last 3 weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below the mean over the last 28 days despite the prior three-week upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has been steadily improving (-62.9 to -51.3), reflecting gradual return-to-office activity that generates incidental weekday retail trips, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -62.9 to -51.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks even though WORKPLACES continues to increase, falsifying the linkage.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS drop-and-rebound (61.3 to 11.9 to 31.1) suggests volatile outdoor-substitution behavior; if PARKS falls below 20 again, households may shift discretionary outings toward indoor retail venues, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from 61.3 to 11.9 then rebounded to 31.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS drop below 20, or falls instead, rejecting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has been gradually declining (24.6 to 21.7), indicating less time spent at home; combined with falling TRANSIT deficits (-68.4 to -63.9), this joint easing of stay-at-home and transit avoidance behavior should interact to amplify RETAIL_REC gains over four weeks beyond what either series predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 24.6 to 21.7 while TRANSIT rose from -68.4 to -63.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks is no greater than what a single-series (RESIDENTIAL-only or TRANSIT-only) linear trend would predict, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility deficit widens by more than 10 points week-on-week, it likely signals a new restriction or public caution event that would simultaneously suppress RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks due to reduced access to commercial districts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change falls below -10 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has ranged between -68.4 and -63.9 over four weeks without such a drop yet
failure_condition: A TRANSIT decline exceeding 10 points occurs without a subsequent decline in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Under a hypothetical reopening regime where WORKPLACES mobility exceeds -50 (near pre-period baseline), eased restrictions on commercial activity would mechanically permit higher RETAIL_REC, as retail capacity limits are correlated with workplace capacity limits in most policy regimes.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at t-0w is -51.3, approaching the -50 threshold
failure_condition: WORKPLACES crosses above -50 but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The PARKS volatility pattern (large week-to-week swings) is consistent with weather-driven seasonal effects; if this volatility persists along with elevated GROCERY_PHARM stability, it suggests a seasonal transition period where outdoor activity substitutes for retail trips, dampening RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung between 11.9 and 61.3 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed between -22.1 and -19.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over four weeks despite continued high PARKS volatility and stable GROCERY_PHARM, indicating no seasonal substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained relatively flat and close to baseline recovery (-21.9 to -20.3) compared to RETAIL_REC's larger deficit, suggesting essential-trip activity has plateaued while discretionary retail still has substantial room to recover, implying continued convergence and RETAIL_REC increase over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within -22.1 to -19.1 while RETAIL_REC moved from -72.6 to -66.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to narrow its gap relative to GROCERY_PHARM over the next four weeks, i.e., the deficit gap stays constant or widens.
